solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way sweetheart goes about showing integrity

indicators.note: the sweetheart's word wraps itself around the abbreviation for way

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment for a loved one
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone's darling takes a route that displays their good character.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrity and this word are synonyms: both name the quality of being truthful and principled.

clue.text: Bird identified by sinful gent originally in Humberside port

indicators.note: the sinful word and the gent's initial go inside the port's name

parts.note: Hull is a port on the Humber estuary in Yorkshire
erring means going astray, sinning

indicators.note: the opening letter of gent is taken

explanation.surface: A bird is picked out by a wicked man in a northern port.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city on the Humber in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: This large grey-and-white seabird is a species of gull, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Novelty we set up in northern loch

indicators.note: the reversed word sits within the northern letter and loch combined

parts.note: Loch Ness is the famous Scottish lake

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means the word we reads upwards

explanation.surface: We create something new at a lake in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelty and this word both mean the quality of being fresh and recent.

clue.text: Repository for damaged harp and capes?

indicators.note: harp and capes are knocked out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: Where a broken harp and torn cloaks are thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges HARP and CAPES; the question mark marks the playful image of a junk pile.
explanation.definitionFit: A dump for discarded waste metal and junk is a store, or repository, for unwanted things.

clue.text: Youth leader ahead of time every twelve months

indicators.note: the leading letter of youth is taken

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: A youth club leader turns up before time each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once a year occurs every twelve months; synonym for annual.

clue.text: Young creature over in Cornish river

indicators.note: the letter for over is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, flowing out at Falmouth
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A young animal is spotted across in a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in the south-west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn horse or donkey is called this, so it is an example of a young creature.

clue.text: Distant agricultural area? 75% of it

indicators.note: three of the four letters of the agricultural word are used, the last left off

parts.note: a farm is land used for agriculture

explanation.surface: A remote rural spot, mostly given over to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to the agricultural area: keep three-quarters of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Far and distant are synonyms for a long way off.

clue.text: Farewell from a girl attached to Brussels?

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
Brussels is the seat of the EU, standing for it as Westminster stands for Parliament

explanation.surface: A goodbye from a woman posted to the European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Brussels hosts the main EU institutions, so it stands for the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a French-derived word for goodbye, used when parting for a long time.

clue.text: Oarsman involved in argument?

definitions.meaning: a person who propels a boat with oars
playfully, a person taking part in a row, or quarrel

explanation.surface: A rower gets into a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Row (rhymes with cow) means a quarrel, so one involved in it is jokily a 'row-er'; the question mark flags the invented word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarsman propels a boat, the same as the first sense; the second is a pun on a quarrel.

clue.text: Publicise young woman's narrow escape in flight

parts.note: to air an idea is to make it public
miss is a young unmarried woman; the 's stands for 'is' linking to the definition

explanation.surface: Telling everyone about a girl's lucky escape aboard a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: An air miss is the term for two aircraft coming dangerously close without colliding: a near collision in the sky.

clue.text: Spectacular number displays formal headgear

parts.note: shows means displays
a topper is a top hat, worn on formal occasions

explanation.surface: A musical's big routine shows off top hats.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or act so impressive it halts the performance for applause; a spectacular number in a show.

clue.text: Diamonds used in specific earrings

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words specific earrings, straddling the gap

explanation.surface: Diamonds feature in some particular earrings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' signals the letters are found inside specifIC Earrings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice is slang for diamonds, from their cold glitter; a crime-novel term for gems.

clue.text: Mostly courteous hanger-on initially obeying Communist executive

indicators.note: most of the word for courteous is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: polite means courteous
a bur is a burr, a seed head that clings, hence a hanger-on

indicators.note: the first letter of obeying is taken

explanation.surface: A deferential hanger-on obeys the party leadership.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of the Soviet Communist Party, its executive body.

clue.text: Fairish new role accepted by board

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are taken inside the word for board

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: role is made anew in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new job given by the directors is only so-so.
explanation.walkthrough: Board as in 'board and lodging' means the meals on the table, not a company's directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairish means moderately good, passable, the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Goods appeal regularly — it's absolutely true, they say

indicators.note: every other letter of the words goods appeal is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for some merchandise, sworn to be perfectly honest.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters 1, 3, 5... of GoOdS aPpEaL gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: People call something they insist is entirely true 'the gospel truth', so the word stands for unquestionable fact.

clue.text: Skives in casual wear

explanation.surface: Someone dodges work while dressed down.
explanation.walkthrough: Skive is British slang for dodging work or school.
explanation.definitionFit: To slack is to shirk, and the plural noun names relaxed trousers worn informally.

clue.text: Animal minder browbeat a woman's daughter

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A stockman bullied some woman's girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browbeat' looks like the main verb, but it is a synonym for COW.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends cattle is a minder of animals, the herding job the word names.

clue.text: A ballad gripping wife and son on every occasion

indicators.note: the letters for a ballad hold the wife's letter within them

parts.note: a lay is a narrative song or poem

explanation.surface: A song that holds a wife and son in its grip every time it is sung.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means at all times, without exception, so on every occasion.

clue.text: A French university in part of London? That's not welcome

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the letter for university goes inside the London district's name

parts.note: Poplar is a district of east London

explanation.surface: A French college in a London district gets a frosty reception.
explanation.walkthrough: POPLAR is a district in east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disliked by most people is unwelcome; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Pensioner carries it over paved area by house

indicators.note: the whole construction is turned over, read upwards in this down answer
the pensioner's letters hold the word it

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: An old person lugs something across a paved yard.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion goes after the first letter, giving OITAP before 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor space beside a house used for sitting.

clue.text: Court with old office at the front

indicators.note: only the opening letter of office is used

explanation.surface: A law court housing an antique office in its frontage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a legal noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to pursue them romantically, a synonym of the verb here.

clue.text: Girl, one tailing bird in meadow

indicators.note: the bird and the one go inside the word for meadow

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: one follows the bird, coming at its tail

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl spots a single bird following another through a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a woman's name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Bill cricketer picked up

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking up raises the cricketer's word to read upwards

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill is paid for a cricketer someone gave a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests a homophone but signals reversal in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tab is American slang for a bar or restaurant bill.

clue.text: Call British prime minister going west

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftward, so the premier's name is written backwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a British prime minister in the 1800s

explanation.surface: Ring a British premier who is heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel was prime minister in the 1830s and 1840s.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager's beep summons its holder, so a bleep is a call to someone.

clue.text: Company doctor's crest

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree; the 's is 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A firm's medic shows off a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock's red crest is called its comb, so the two words share that sense.

clue.text: Thin coil finally used in transmitter

indicators.note: the chosen letter is placed inside the word for transmitter

parts.note: a sender is something that transmits

indicators.note: the end letter of coil is taken

explanation.surface: A slender coil is the last component fitted into a radio transmitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender and thin are synonyms describing something narrow or slight.
